function.name: chat_completions
function.description: Processes a series of user messages and generates a chat completion using a specified language model. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

messages.description: An array of user message objects, where each message can be a simple string or a structured object containing blocks of text.

model.description: The identifier of the language model to be used for generating completions.

max_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion.

stop_sequences.description: Optional sequences where the model should stop generating further tokens.

function.name: generate_image
function.description: Asynchronously generates an image based on a given prompt and returns the URLs of the generated images. It handles request size limits and includes a timeout for the generation process. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

prompt.description: The prompt based on which the image will be generated.

request_id.description: A unique identifier for the generation request, automatically generated using UUID4.

model.description: The model used for image generation. If not specified, a default model is used.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for image generation before timing out. This is a float type value.

client_max_size.description: The maximum size of the request in bytes.

function.name: generate_completion
function.description: Generates a text completion based on a given prompt and model input, with a specified maximum number of tokens. Supports various AI models. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

prompt.description: The input text prompt to generate completion from.

model_input.description: The model to be used for generating the completion.

max_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens to generate.

assist.description: The type of assistance provided by the AI model.

function.name: generation_claude
function.description: Generates a message using the Claude model with specified parameters, such as the prompt and model configuration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

prompt.description: The input text prompt to guide the generation of the message.

model.description: The specific Claude model variant to use for generation, e.g., 'claude-3-haiku-20240307'.

max_tokens.description: The maximum number of tokens to generate for the message.

assist.description: Flag to enable or disable assistance mode in the generation.

temperature.description: Controls the randomness of the generation. 0 is deterministic. This is a float type value.

system.description: The system or framework being used for the message generation.

That error usually pops up when you try to treat a `Message` object like a dictionary or list—e.g., `msg['text']` or `msg[0]`—but the class doesn’t implement the `__getitem__` method. Here’s a quick checklist to help you pinpoint the issue: | Step | What to Check | Why | |------|---------------|-----| | 1 | **Inspect the `Message` class** | Does it define `__getitem__`? If not, you can’t subscript it. | | 2 | **Look at the code where the error occurs** | Identify the exact line that’s causing the problem. | | 3 | **Use attribute access instead** | If the message has attributes like `msg.text`, use that. | | 4 | **Convert to a dict if needed** | `msg_dict = msg.__dict__` (or a custom method) then subscript. | | 5 | **Check for library updates** | Some libraries change the API; maybe you’re using an older version. | | 6 | **Add a `__getitem__` method** | If you control the class, you can add something like:
`def __getitem__(self, key): return getattr(self, key)` | If you can share the snippet where the error happens, I can give more targeted advice. In the meantime, try replacing any subscripting (`msg['field']`) with attribute access (`msg.field`) or converting the object to a dictionary first.
